items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-11-10
items.q: We had Monk Hazel playing mellophone. Ray Benitez was playing bass.

ctx.x: Four drummers? At the same time?

The Six Beasts Band, it was four drummers. We had Monk Hazel playing mellophone. Ray Benitez was playing bass. Jack Otto was playing piano. Jack Otto was playing drums. And I was playing piano, who was also a drummer. And I was the name of Colomaz, who was a alto, a tenor saxophone player. That was the band. They had four drummers. And all of them playing different instruments. I mean, Monk was playing the mellophone. Not French horn, he played mellophone.

items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-20
items.q: Doc died. Three bass players that worked with me the past 10 years.

ctx.x: Did Stranicos ever go over to the Gulf Coast? He was from the Gulf Coast.

Ellis was from the Gulf Coast. Yeah. It was Stranicos' man that we used to play over there with Charlie Wagner, Johnny Roniger, Meyer Weinberg, Doc Benitez. You know, he died recently. Oh, yes, he did, yeah. Doc died. Three bass players that worked with me the past 10 years. All died in a very short period of time.
Yes, sir. Who was the ottoman?
